newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM sees 5-6 pct GDP growth in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM sees 5-6 pct GDP growth in 1998.

text.p: Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Monday he expected Poland's gross domestic product to grow by 5-6 percent next year -- a slightly more optimistic forecast then the so far expected 5-5.5 percent.
"We can say that economic growth next year will be five to six percent," Cimoszewicz told reporters before a cabinet debate on the macroeconomic assumptions of the 1998 national budget.
The government forecasts this year's GDP growth at 5.5 percent after a six percent rise in 1996. @
Cimoszewicz said Poland's main economic challenge next year would be to keep the fast growing trade gap under control but added that the deficit has not reached dangerous levels yet.
The trade gap after the first four months of the year was $4 billion against $2 billion in the same period of last year.
"The deficit has not yet reached an alarming level -- it is assumed that a gap of seven percent of GDP is such a dangerous level and we now have four percent...," Cimoszewicz said.
Cimoszewicz also said that security and education would be the 1998 budget's priorities.
